items.prompt: The prefix pre- means before. What does preheat mean?

options.why: Again is the meaning of re-.
Not is the meaning of un- or dis-.
Wrongly is the meaning of mis-.

hints: Look at the two parts of the word.
Cover pre- and read what is left.
Put the meaning of pre- together with heat.
items.explanation: Pre- means before. To preheat an oven means to heat it before you start cooking.

items.prompt: The prefix mis- means wrongly. What does misspell mean?

options.why: Again is the meaning of re-.
Before is the meaning of pre-.
Mis- means wrongly, not never.

hints: Find the prefix at the start of the word.
Cover mis- and read what is left.
Put the meaning of mis- together with spell.
items.explanation: Mis- means wrongly, so misspell means spell a word wrongly.

items.prompt:
Add mis- or pre- to counted.
Tom ___ the eggs, so he thought there were seven, not six.
hints: Did Tom get the right number?
Which prefix means wrongly?
Write the prefix, then the whole word counted.
items.explanation: Tom counted wrongly, so he miscounted. Mis- means wrongly.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
hints: Find the prefix in each word.
Pre- means before. Mis- means wrongly or badly.
Start with prepay. Which meaning has before in it and is about money?
items.explanation: Pre- means before, so prepay means pay before. Mis- means wrongly or badly, so misbehave means behave badly.

items.prompt: Sort the words. Which prefix makes a real word?
hints: Say each word with each prefix in front of it.
Only one of these prefixes makes a real word each time.
Start with spell. Is it prespell, misspell, unspell or disspell?
items.explanation: We say preheat and preview, misspell and misbehave, unfair and unlucky, disagree and disobey.

items.prompt: Before the film, our teacher showed us a short ___ so we knew what it was about.

options.why: Misview is not a word.
Unview is not a word.
Disview is not a word.

hints: The teacher showed it before the film.
Which prefix means before?
Try each prefix in front of view. Which one is a word you have heard?
items.explanation: Pre- means before. A preview is a short look at something before you see all of it.

items.prompt: Kemal ___ the question, so his answer was about the wrong thing.

options.why: Reread means read again. That would help him get it right!
Preread is not a word we use.
Unread means not read yet.

hints: What went wrong with Kemal's answer?
He read the question, but not in the right way.
Which prefix means wrongly?
items.explanation: Misread means read wrongly. Kemal misread the question, so his answer was about the wrong thing.

items.prompt:
Add mis- or pre- to behave.
Please do not ___ in the library.
hints: How should you act in a library?
You need a word that means behave badly.
Which prefix means wrongly or badly?
items.explanation: Misbehave means behave badly. Mis- means wrongly or badly.

items.prompt: Choose all the words where pre- means before.

options.why: Pre is just part of pretty. Tty is not a word.
Press is one whole word. Ss is not a word.
Prey is an animal hunted by another. Y is not a word.

hints: Cover pre at the start of each word.
Is the rest a real word?
If it is, check that before makes sense with it.
items.explanation: Preheat means heat before, preview means see before, and prehistoric means before history was written down. In pretty, press and prey, pre is just part of the word.

items.prompt: Ella ___ her keys and could not find them anywhere.

options.why: Replaced means put back, or swapped for a new one.
Preplaced is not a word we use.
Displaced means pushed out of its place. We need a word for lost.

hints: What happened to Ella's keys?
She put them somewhere, but in the wrong place.
Which prefix means wrongly?
items.explanation: Misplaced means put in the wrong place and lost. Mis- means wrongly.

items.prompt: Which word has a prefix that means wrongly?

options.why: Mist is one whole word. T is not a word.
Miss is one whole word.
Mister is one whole word. Ter is not a word.

hints: Cover mis at the start of each word.
Is the rest a real word?
If the rest is a word, does wrongly make sense with it?
items.explanation: Mishear is mis + hear, and it means hear wrongly. In mist, miss and mister, the letters mis are just part of the word.

items.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?

options.why: Keep all of mis- and all of spell: mis + spell.
Spell ends with a double l.
There is only one p in spell.

hints: Think about the two parts of the word.
Write the prefix, then the root word, without dropping any letters.
Count the letter s where the two parts join.
items.explanation: Mis + spell = misspell. The prefix keeps its s and spell keeps its s, so there are two s letters together.

items.prompt: The prefix un- usually means not. What does unhappy mean?

options.why: Un- does not make a word stronger. It turns it round.
Again is a different prefix, re-.
Before is a different prefix, pre-.

hints: Look at the start of the word.
Un- changes the meaning to the opposite idea.
Say the prefix meaning, then the root word.
items.explanation: Un- means not, so unhappy means not happy.

items.prompt: Which word means to build something again?

options.why: Unbuild is not a word. Un- would mean not.
Mis- means wrongly, not again.
Disbuild is not a real word.

hints: Which prefix means again?
Think of re- as a replay button.
Put each prefix in front of build and check it makes sense.
items.explanation: Re- means again, so rebuild means to build again.

items.prompt: The knot was very tight, so Hadi tried to ___ it.
hints: Did Hadi want to make the knot or undo it?
Un- can mean to undo something.
Say the sentence with each word and listen.
items.explanation: Untie means to undo a knot. Un- here means to reverse an action.

items.prompt:
Add re- to read.
Maya liked the story so much that she ___ it twice.
hints: Which prefix gives the idea of again?
Write the prefix first.
Write re-, then read, with no space or hyphen.
items.explanation: Reread means to read again. Re- means again.

items.prompt: Match each prefix to its meaning.
hints: Think of one word for each prefix.
Unlucky, replay and misspell can help you.
Start with pre-. Think of preheat.
items.explanation: Un- means not, re- means again, mis- means wrongly, pre- means before and dis- means the opposite of.

items.prompt: Sort the words by the prefix that makes a real word.
hints: Try each prefix with each word.
Say the new word aloud. Does it sound real?
Start with appear. Is it unappear, inappear or disappear?
items.explanation: We say unsafe and unwell, incorrect and invisible, dislike and disappear.

items.prompt: In which word is un- a prefix meaning not?

options.why: Uncle is one whole word. Cle is not a word.
Unit is one whole word. It is not about not.
Until is a different word. Til is not a word.

hints: Cover un- and read the rest.
Is the rest a real word?
Then check that not makes sense with it.
items.explanation: Happy is a real word and un- makes it mean not happy. In the other words, un is just part of the word.

items.prompt: Build a sentence. Use the word that means heat again.
hints: Look for the word that fits the soup.
Which prefix means again?
Start with the first word that begins with a capital letter.
items.explanation: Re- means again, so reheat means to heat again.

items.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly and means not possible?

options.why: Before p, in- changes to im-.
Unpossible is not a real word.
Dispossible is not a real word.

hints: Think about the letter that comes after the prefix.
Some prefixes change before certain letters.
Say each word. Which one is a word you have heard?
items.explanation: Impossible uses im- because the next letter is p. Im- means not.

items.prompt:
Add dis- to appear.
The magician made the rabbit ___.
hints: Which prefix means the opposite of?
Join the prefix to appear.
Check that you keep both p letters.
items.explanation: Disappear means to go out of sight. Dis- means the opposite of, and appear keeps both p letters.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses a prefix wrongly?

options.why: This one is fine. Recheck means check again.
This one is fine. Mislaid means put in the wrong place.
This one is fine. Disagree means not agree.

hints: Read each sentence slowly.
Which word do you never hear?
Say the root word and the prefix together.
items.explanation: We say impossible, not unpossible. The other prefixed words are real.

items.prompt: In which word does un- mean to undo, not not?

options.why: Here un- means not kind.
Here un- means not fair.
Here un- means not safe.

hints: Some un- words describe an action.
Which word is something you do?
Check which word is a verb.
items.explanation: Untie is an action that reverses tying. In the other words, un- just means not.

items.prompt: Choose all the words where re- means again.

options.why: Re is just part of real. Al is not a word.
Re is just part of reason. Ason is not a word.
Remember is a whole word. It does not mean member again.

hints: Cover re- and look at what is left.
Is the rest a real word that fits?
Then check that again makes sense.
items.explanation: Rewind is wind again, restart is start again and recycle is use again. In real, reason and remember, re- is not a prefix meaning again.

items.prompt:
Add mis- or re- to read.
Kofi ___ the sign at first. Then he ___ it slowly and understood.
hints: Did Kofi understand the sign at first?
Wrongly is mis-. Again is re-.
Fill the first gap, then the second.
items.explanation: Kofi read the sign wrongly, so he misread it. Then he read it again, so he reread it.

items.prompt: Which two words use different prefixes that both mean not?

options.why: These use the same prefix, re-, and it means again.
These use the same prefix, mis-, and it means wrongly.
These use the same prefix, pre-, and it means before.

hints: Find the pair with two different prefixes.
Then check each one means not.
Cross out the pairs that repeat a prefix.
items.explanation: Un- and im- both mean not. The other pairs use the same prefix twice.

items.prompt: Spell the word that means to go out of sight.
items.sentence: The rabbit began to disappear into the hat.
hints: It starts with a prefix.
The root has two p letters.
Say it in three parts: dis, ap, pear.
items.explanation: Disappear is dis- plus appear. Keep both p letters from appear.

items.prompt: Spell the word that means not needed.
items.sentence: It is unnecessary to take an umbrella today.
hints: It starts with the prefix un-.
The root word has one c and two s letters.
Say the root in parts: nec, es, sary.
items.explanation: Unnecessary is un- plus necessary. Necessary has one c and two s letters.

items.prompt: True or false: The prefix mis- can mean wrongly, as in the word misspell.
hints: A prefix goes at the start of a word.
Think of misunderstand, which means to understand wrongly.
Mis- changes the meaning to wrongly.
items.explanation: Mis- means wrongly or badly. To misspell is to spell a word wrongly.

items.prompt: True or false: The prefix pre- means after, as in the word preview.
hints: Think of preheat the oven.
You preheat an oven before you cook.
Pre- means the opposite of post-.
items.explanation: Pre- means before. A preview is a look at something before it is shown to everyone.

items.prompt: True or false: Adding dis- to the word agree makes disagree, which has the opposite meaning.
hints: Look at what dis- does to the base word.
Dis- often means not or the opposite of.
Agree and disagree are opposites.
items.explanation: Dis- often reverses the meaning of a word. Agree becomes disagree.

items.prompt: True or false: The word misplace means to put something in exactly the right place.
hints: Break the word into mis- and place.
What does mis- do to a word?
Think of misplacing your pencil case.
items.explanation: Misplace means to put something in the wrong place, or to lose it for a while. Mis- means wrongly.

items.prompt: Add mis- to spell: ___.
hints: Mis means wrongly.
Keep both s letters.
mis + spell
items.explanation: Mis + spell makes misspell, with two s letters.
